title: Owner's plan corrections: the whole-transcript ceiling, and OD-12's placement rule
body:
**Needs your approval** — both files are CODEOWNERS-held. **Two documents, nothing else in the diff.**

---

## `docs/plans/whole-transcript-threshold.md` — items **G** / BL-20, OD-13, OD-19

**Its one open uncertainty is answered: NO upper bound.** You ruled it on 2026-08-19, OD-13 recorded it as R1008 superseding OD-5/R1001, and the plan still said *"pending — do not build this slice until it is answered"* while the answer had been on the default branch for four days.

The lumpy-spend concern the uncertainty was filed against is handled at its source rather than by a ceiling: with R5's clustering and R1000's re-cut, the sparse long stream that would have produced the lumpy request never reaches the 80% ratio at all.

**The ratio is now stated as measured on RE-CUT text.** When this plan was written, `merge_overlapping` concatenated overlapping windows, so the numerator counted the overlap once per window — **11.7x on the real corpus**, which would have pushed almost every video over the 80% line and made this rule fire everywhere. R1000 is what makes the ratio mean what the plan says it means.

**A banner at the top says slice 1 must not be built, and why.** The routing is being built under `docs/plans/oracle/capped-whole-transcript-path.md`, whose slug is an **address rather than a description** — that document was rewritten on 2026-08-20 and specifies the *uncapped* path. OD-19 already records the prohibition in the design layer, where the review gate reads it; this puts it where a reader of the plan sees it first.

**It stays `status: draft` and is not deleted**, which is what you asked for. BL-20, OD-13 and OD-19 all cite it by name, and a missing file those decisions point at would confuse the next reader more than a superseded one that says so. It becomes `status: merged` when R1008's work actually lands — that field means "the work shipped, by another route", and claiming it now would be false.

*(A plan must keep at least one slice — `plan-parse.sh` rejects one with none — so dropping slice 1 outright was not available.)*

---

## `docs/plans/corpus-and-checkpoint.md` — item **H** / OD-12, and OD-11's correction

**Every shared type and exception in the ledger's Signatures block now names its module.** OD-12 was filed against this very slice: two blind authors agreed on the ledger's behaviour and disagreed on where its types go, so the orchestrator's shared contract assigned modules ad hoc and put `FetchFailure` in `transcripts.py` — circular, because the ledger is what the transcript stage reports failures **to**.

This ratifies `FetchFailure`, `HaltTriggered` and `Ledger` in `ledger.py`, where the built tree already has them, and states that the `transcripts.py` re-export shim retires. **Removing the shim is code and gets its own pull request**; what this does is stop specifying the placement the shim papers over.

Two references to `data/aliases.toml` become the configured `alias_table_path` and the repository-root `aliases.toml`, which OD-11/R1007 moved it to.

---

Both plans still parse (`plan-lint`: 15 of 15). 757 tests passing, unchanged — no code in this diff.
